costGuide.title: Mercedes-Benz M113.990 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an M113.990 engine typically takes 12-16 hours at £75-£95/hr (AMG specialist) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this specific engine is the condition of the Eaton M112 supercharger (specifically the coupler and snout bearings), the crankshaft position sensor (CPS), and the valley cover gasket. Because the M113.990 is a high-performance AMG unit, recon specialists will typically replace the supercharger coupler as standard, fit a new CPS, and renew all brittle valve cover and oil seals to prevent immediate post-installation failures. For a full breakdown of market rates, see our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Mercedes-Benz M113.990 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Supercharger Coupler Degradation
items.whatHappens: The Eaton M112 supercharger uses a plastic/rubber isolator coupler to connect the front drive pulley to the internal rotors. Over time, this coupler disintegrates, resulting in a loud rattling, clunking, or whining noise from the front of the engine and a complete loss of boost pressure.
items.repairVsReplace: The coupler can be replaced independently as a relatively inexpensive maintenance item. However, if ignored, the resulting vibration can damage the snout bearings, requiring a full supercharger rebuild or replacement.

items.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor (CPS) Failure
items.whatHappens: The CPS is located at the rear of the engine block, near the firewall, where it is exposed to extreme heat cycles from the turbo/supercharger and exhaust manifolds. The internal wiring degrades, causing the sensor to fail when the engine is hot, resulting in sudden stalling or a no-start condition.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the CPS is a relatively inexpensive and straightforward repair, though access is tight. It is highly recommended to replace the sensor proactively during any major engine service.

items.title: Valley Cover Gasket Leak
items.whatHappens: The plastic valley cover gasket (located between the two cylinder heads) hardens and shrinks over time, allowing oil to leak directly into the spark plug wells. This causes misfires, rough idling, and can eventually lead to ignition coil failure.
items.repairVsReplace: This is a routine maintenance item. Replacing the valley cover gasket and spark plug tube seals is relatively inexpensive in terms of parts, though it requires removing the intake manifold and supercharger assembly for proper access.

items.title: Balance Shaft Gear Wear
items.whatHappens: The balance shafts, designed to smooth out V8 vibrations, are driven by small gears that can wear or shear over time. This triggers crankshaft position sensor error codes, causes a rough idle, and in severe cases, broken gear fragments can jam the oil pump.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the balance shaft assembly and gears is a known, albeit labour-intensive, repair. If the oil pump or timing has been compromised, a full reconditioned M113.990 unit is required.

failures.goodYearsLine: The M113.990 is widely regarded as one of the most durable and reliable high-performance V8 engines ever produced. Units maintained with strict oil change intervals and timely supercharger coupler replacements routinely exceed 150,000 miles without major internal bottom-end issues .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes-Benz M113.990
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block, near the oil filter housing. It will also be listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or visible via a VIN decode. The M113.990 is a highly specific, single-application engine code. It is sometimes confused with the naturally aspirated M113.960 (5.0L) or the supercharged M113.980/970 found in the S-Class, CL-Class, and SL-Class. Fitting the wrong revision or assuming interchangeability matters significantly: the M113.990 features specific W211 E 55 AMG engine mounts, a unique supercharger intake plenum, specific ECU mapping, and distinct wiring harness routing that will not function correctly if swapped with other M113 variants without extensive and costly modification.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement M113.990 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used M113.990 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and documented proof of a recent supercharger coupler replacement, valley cover gasket replacement, and CPS replacement. Given the performance nature of the W211 E 55 AMG, buying a used unit with unknown history is a significant financial risk.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned M113.990 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by replacing the supercharger coupler, fitting a new CPS, replacing the balance shaft assembly (if required), and renewing all brittle valve cover and oil seals, giving the engine a fresh, reliable lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full M113.990 engine rebuild is highly justified for low-mileage or collector W211 E 55 AMG restorations where originality, matching numbers, and maximum longevity are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your M113.990 engine is installed by specialists familiar with AMG V8 and Kompressor systems, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the M113.990 is exclusively found in the W211 E 55 AMG, a model whose values are currently appreciating and typically range from £8,000 to £25,000+ depending on condition and mileage, a full replacement is generally financially viable and protects the asset's value. However, if the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate the investment carefully .
